advice: Experiment: split the reduction into fixed-size FP32 K blocks in the existing SME multiply loop. For each output tile, keep all four ZA accumulators live across the full reduction, but iterate k0 from 0 to n in blocks (for example, 32), with an inner loop over k0..min(k0+32,n). Preserve increasing-k update order, the current full transpose layout, selectors 0..3, and the general predicated tail path. This is a loop-structure experiment only; it adds no packing or allocation. Hypothesis: making reduction ranges explicit may help the compiler schedule address updates and loads. There is no supplied evidence that cache blocking will help, so treat cache benefit as unknown. Compare against the existing source with fresh serial AC controls under the fixed benchmark. Check FP32 tolerance 0.002, odd and small n, n<=0 behavior, bounds at the final K block, and confirm the benchmark configuration is unchanged. Do not attribute any joint score to this experiment unless it is measured separately.
risks: The compiler may emit the same code or add loop overhead; a block size of 32 is an experiment parameter, not a known optimum. Numerical results may differ slightly if compiler scheduling changes, so verify the fixed error limit. No speedup or cache bottleneck is established by the supplied noisy historical scores.
